candidates.finding: Check if a ConcurrentWorkflow cancelled/failed task leaves its task-key DashSet reservation and blocks later legitimate work.
candidates.screening_result: Original `main@ee1e74cb6e2c94775db88dddb311f2235e3fe9e3` (same as October Index pin), Apache-2.0. First-party ConcurrentWorkflow::run inserts the task key only after empty-agent/task guard, immediately binds it to RunningTask, and `impl Drop for RunningTask` removes the key on all normal Rust future return/drop/unwind paths. The proposed persistent reservation after failed/cancelled same-key task is prevented by this RAII guard. No source-native failing reproducer or patch; no Rust suite claimed.

candidates.finding: Check if custom/aliased background delegate may be admitted despite built-in mutating effects on the shared checkout.
candidates.screening_result: Original `main@3be6ff94b5e7adfee30f5ead8972dbdbbb5c4319` differs from October pin, MIT. Current built-in spawn subagent classifies read-only agent tools via registry effect metadata; writable background/isolate only runs concurrently when isolation is available. On isolation-open failure it refuses background writer with explicit error; foreground mutable execution receives an alone/serial permit. The predicted supported writable background escape has no first-party evidence. No native Rust test or patch executed.

candidates.finding: Check whether closing an active PeerTask and promoting FIFO allows a concurrent admission to accept a second active task for the same agent pair.
candidates.screening_result: Current onecli `main@90e874c0cf4e059401577f687bee93e9f376bc65`, Apache-2.0 core with separately enterprise-licensed paths. First-party peer-task-service.ts declares a one-open-per-pair partial unique index; opening races use uniqueness-error handling, queued promotion is conditional `updateMany WHERE status=queued` and handles unique collision as a lost race. The hypothesized two simultaneous active pair tasks is already fenced; no native counterexample or patch. CLA.md explicitly treats *submitting contributions* as personal CLA acceptance, so any future proposed external PR requires valid contributor-person legal authorization beyond routine publication mandate.
